facts.text: UL 4600 explains how to build and judge a safety case for a product that makes decisions autonomously, by specifying topics and questions the case must answer.
facts.quote: UL 4600 is a standard that explains how to build and judge a safety case for a product that makes decisions on its own, by setting out a long list of topics and questions the case must answer.

facts.text: The third edition of UL 4600, Standard for Safety for the Evaluation of Autonomous Products, is dated 17 March 2023 and was written for self-driving vehicles and robots.
facts.quote: UL 4600, Standard for Safety for the Evaluation of Autonomous Products, third edition of 17 March 2023, was written for self-driving vehicles and robots [Chapters 10, 12].

facts.text: UL 4600 prescribes no design or test.
facts.quote: It prescribes no design or test.

facts.text: UL 4600 requires a safety case to address or explicitly argue away prompts covering hazards, operating domain, perception, machine learning, metrics, field feedback and other topics; conformance is judged by the completeness of those responses.
facts.quote: For each topic (hazards, operating domain, perception, machine learning, metrics, field feedback and more) it gives prompts the safety case must address or explicitly argue away, and conformance is judged on how completely that is done.

facts.text: The booklet identifies UL 4600, ISO 21448 and ISO/PAS 8800 as sources of assurance structures for machine-learning-based and autonomous safety functions.
facts.quote: The booklet names UL 4600, with ISO 21448 and ISO/PAS 8800, as a source of assurance structures for machine-learning-based and autonomous safety functions [Chapter 1]

facts.text: The booklet uses UL 4600 question lists as one template for the final validation plan.
facts.quote: uses its question lists as one template for the final plan [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The booklet did not examine UL 4600's content on simulation credibility.
facts.quote: the standard's content on simulation credibility was not examined [Chapter 10].

facts.text: An automatic brake on an operator-driven machine is not an autonomous product, so UL 4600 can help make its safety case complete but is not a route to conformity.
facts.quote: An automatic brake on an operator-driven machine is not an autonomous product, so UL 4600 is a way to make the case complete, not a route to conformity.

facts.text: UL 4600 questions about perception, operating domain and field feedback map onto the hardest problems of the heavy off-road automatic-braking validation program.
facts.quote: Its questions about perception, operating domain and field feedback map onto the hardest problems of this program

facts.text: No off-road body has adopted UL 4600.
facts.quote: no off-road body has adopted it

facts.text: The heavy off-road automatic-braking validation plan should borrow UL 4600's thoroughness without claiming compliance.
facts.quote: the plan should borrow its thoroughness without claiming compliance.
